title: Inside Lukas Swid's Journey Building Helcyon AI: The Health Monitoring Platform for Business
summary: Inside Lukas Swid's Journey Building Helcyon AI: The Health Monitoring Platform for Business
body_markdown:
Many startups and small businesses don’t survive longer than five years. Governments and institutions often write the failure rate off as the risk of starting a business.


But businesses rarely fail suddenly. Rather, the conditions that lead to their undoing develop slowly and silently, buried in the thousands of transactions that busy owners don’t have time to read. Traditional financial reports help you understand why a business failed in retrospect, but do little to prevent failure from happening.


With over 25 years of experience running businesses across chemicals, payments, food, and construction, seasoned business leader[Lukas Swid](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lukasswid/) recognized that it’s usually what owners don’t know that causes their business to fail. So he set out to build[Helcyon AI](https://helcyon.ai/) and make it easier for owners to catch business health warning signs before they become irreversible.


## Introducing Helcyon AI: Health Monitoring for Your Business


Helcyon is a financial intelligence platform that reads transaction-level financial data, detects changes against the business’s own normal operating patterns, and reveals insights into cash, margins, obligations, and forward cash position.


While tools like QuickBooks and Xero look at aggregated documents like the P&L and balance sheet to determine whether performance is up or down, Helcyon reviews every single transaction and interprets performance from the ground up. “The whole reason for Helcyon to exist,” Lukas explains, “is to tell you exactly what is hurting your business at the moment it starts to occur, so that you can respond quickly and do something about it.”


The platform is designed to focus on five key business vital signs: Cash Pulse (liquidity, runway, cash trajectory), Revenue Blood Pressure (stability, concentration, pricing power), Margin Temperature (margins, cost pressure, unit economics), Customer Heartbeat (retention, concentration, customer behavior), and Growth Oxygen (reinvestment, capacity, growth efficiency). And unlike traditional financial platforms that report what has already happened, Helcyon detects changes as they happen, enabling business owners to take action as trends emerge.


Helcyon has been very intentional about how AI is used in the platform, Lukas explains. “AI is not a reliable source for financial truth, as it makes mistakes and often changes its mind about an interpretation. Helcyon is completely coded, its financial results are produced by code, and the assembly of the report is done by AI.”


## Lukas’s Journey to Helcyon AI


Before founding Helcyon, Lukas had built a notable career that included 16+ years in the chemical industry during which he served as managing director of international business at[Vantage](https://www.vantagegrp.com/en/) , overseeing around 20 companies across 29 countries.


As part of the role, Lukas stood in front of the Vantage board every month to report performance. If results were good, he’d be asked whether they were reliable enough to budget on. If results weren’t good, he’d be asked what had caused it and what the cure was.


Part of the challenge was that Lukas never felt he could take a general manager’s report at face value. Before presenting results to the board, he had to spend countless hours verifying them with analysts and teams across the business.


In his own businesses beyond Vantage, one in food and another in construction, he continued to feel the same pain. “Even good, honest managers make mistakes,” says Lukas. “They have biases, and if you always trust them and don’t verify, you may get into trouble later. But verifying claims in the data can be difficult and take a lot of time.” And in his payment processing company, Lukas saw merchants with seemingly healthy businesses disappear three or six months later. The warning signs were always in the data, but nobody was reading them.


Recognizing that these key business health insights were being overlooked, Lukas set out to build Helcyon with the aim of revealing precisely what is impacting business health, with proof and timestamps.


Now two years into the journey, Lukas and his engineering team are finalizing the platform, currently focused on what he describes as "testing the platform’s engines to ensure it can survive severe turbulence." Lukas is aiming for a full launch of Helcyon in February 2027 with hiring to follow soon after.


## Lukas’s Advice for Fellow business owners


Throughout his career, Lukas has driven his success by going all-in on what he’s building. business owners have to be obsessed, he says. “If you’re not obsessed with it, if you’re not devoting all of your time, even going to the bathroom thinking about it, you are not going to be successful. Until the business is launched and flourishing, you need to be consistent.”


Part of getting to that point of flourishing is knowing how to develop a resilient product. Lukas recommends business owners try to break what they’re building. “When you’re building a business, it is important to try to break it. Try everything and see what breaks. business owners can avoid trying to break what they’re building and hope that it will be okay. That is the wrong approach. Sometimes you may get lucky; most of the time you do not.”


To learn more about Lukas’s journey building Helcyon AI, you can[follow Lukas on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/lukasswid/) and visit[Helcyon.ai](http://helcyon.ai/) .
